doc.title: Ted Piltzecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 10, 2019

title: How he got the George Shearing Quintet audition
summary: Marian McPartland remembered him sitting in at Eastman, and Shearing's manager called him for an audition; he landed the job.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: No. I like this stuff. Because other people will like it, not just music fans, other profs etcetera. Okay. So you’ve got a long list of people that have played with you and people that you’ve played with and I wanted to ask you about how George Shearing came into your life.

It sort of was a surprise. When I was at Eastman Marian McPartland came through with her trio. It was Rick Petrone and Joe Corsello the other members. And they gave a little workshop and I sat in on the vibraphone and that was — to call it basic would be a polite description. I mean I didn’t know anything. I was pretty Neanderthal on the instrument at that time. I learned, I got more finesse later. But she remembered it, so George needed a vibraphone player for a quintet a year or two later and I guess he called Marian, and I’m in my apartment in New York and I get a call and it’s George Shearing’s manager and he’s coming to do the “Today Show” would you like to audition for the quintet tomorrow? I said, “Great, sure, why not. Who’s George Shearing?” I mean I’d heard of George Gershwin. I was such a neophyte and then I quickly, you know immediately learned all about Berlin and started looking at “Conception,” oh my God, I’ve got to play this stuff? And I found out very quickly and I showed up and managed to play well enough to get the gig. So like the next week I’m in Los Angeles, you know, playing with the quintet and I’m just about shaking in my boots because, you know, and that’s how I learned about this. Then I realized that incredible contribution and the long legacy of this guy’s career. And even later I’ll tell you more stories, but the depth of his ability was really quite remarkable. So I’m in the quintet and we used to play, you know, the music, if you look at the music, you don’t have to learn everything but the music stand
